# Review depth

## 1. Scope

Read the change and the code it touches before judging it. Trace each changed function to its callers and note every caller whose behavior changes. A review that only reads the diff misses the caller that relied on the old behavior.

## 2. Correctness

For each changed branch, name an input that reaches it and the output it produces. Check empty, single-element, boundary and malformed inputs. When a default or initial value is removed, state what happens on the first iteration and on empty input.

## 3. Evidence

Separate what you ran from what you inferred. Quote the command or the test name for anything you claim to have verified. Do not say tests are missing until you have searched for them and can name where you looked.

## 4. Severity

Rank findings: blocking defects first, then risks, then style. Give each finding a concrete failure scenario. Drop any finding you cannot tie to a scenario.

## 5. Reporting

End the review with a short verdict, the findings in rank order, and a list of what was not checked. Keep the verdict to one sentence.
